data.name: Battle For The Hill
data.detailed_description:
🏛️ Battle for the Hill

A free-to-play, persistent multiplayer political strategy game. Build a politician, win elections, pass laws, lead parties, run corporations, shape the courts, and fight for power in a living democracy that keeps ticking whether you are online or not.

Create a character. Pick your country and home region. Choose your ideology. Then compete against real players for offices, money, influence, and control of the state.

Early Access. Free to play. The world does not pause for you.

👤 Forge a Political Career

Create a politician with custom ideology, identity, and background

Climb the ladder: local races, state legislature, statewide office, national legislature, Cabinet, courts, or the top executive seat

Manage Campaign Strength, State Reputation, National Reputation, National Prestige, and Party Strength

Spend Political Capital on the actions that move the map

Raise money through PAC and grassroots fundraising

Run ads and attack ads to shape public perception

Pay the price for carpetbagging or switching parties: reputation, donors, and trust are not free

🗳️ Win the Vote

Contest primaries and general elections on a persistent schedule

Compete for endorsements that can tip close races

Fight presidential and national leadership contests where your country supports them

Face AI candidates that keep low-population races alive until humans step in

Invest in Competitive Party Strength Organization to harden your party's edge in key states

🤝 Parties, Caucuses, and Power Blocs

Join a major party or help build and administer one

Organize at the national and state level with chairs, treasuries, and leadership races

Join or found caucuses to coordinate players who share your lane

Use whip tools, agenda control, and party discipline to keep your side in line

Turn factions into machines: money, votes, messaging, and loyalty

📜 Write the Law

Draft, debate, and pass bills in national legislatures

Work state legislatures with real state-law outcomes

Whip votes, cut cross-party deals, and survive veto politics

Shape election rules, policy stances, and the legal environment your rivals have to campaign under

⚖️ Executive Power and the Courts

Serve as President, Prime Minister, Chancellor, Governor, or other country-specific executive roles

Appoint and run Cabinet portfolios with localized titles and institutions

Influence appointments, budgets, and national direction from the executive

Shape outcomes from the high court through appointments, challenges, and precedent

Deliver official addresses and set the public narrative from the top

💰 Corporations and the Live Economy

Run party-linked corporations with treasuries, CEOs, shares, and bonds

Claim and grow sectors across industries in a ticking market

Trade the stock market, hold bonds and gold, and track personal net worth

Manage national and state budgets as fiscal pressure hits the political system

Watch commodity markets and cross-country economic pressure change the board

Engage labor through union systems tied into the wider economy

🏙️ State and Local Government

Play the map: each region is a battleground for parties, elections, laws, and money

Govern as a state executive with appointments, election rules, and stance tools

Push state budgets, ministries, and policy that feed into national politics

Use state-level enforcement and administration tools that change how your region runs

📰 Media, Messaging, and Social Play

Publish news articles and run publications with subscribers and audience

Post Chirps, build narrative, and fight the information war in public

Message rivals and allies, track notifications, and manage your political inbox

Deploy player ads and keep your brand in front of voters

Shape corporate news as business and politics collide

🌍 A Wider World

Explore a world map and nations list beyond a single capital

Play primarily in deep simulations like the United States, with additional countries and localized institutions available as the sim expands

Face country-specific government structures: presidential systems, Westminster politics, cabinets, chambers, and titles that match the nation

Engage diplomacy, ambassadors, treaties, and wars from the defense and foreign-policy layer

Participate in international organizations and world-leader statements

Climb political and wealth scoreboards against players across the map

🪖 Military Influence

Build military influence and branch standing as a parallel path to prestige

Engage national military pages, budgets, and equipment systems where available

Use defense power as leverage, not as the only way to win

🎲 Side Games and Meta Systems

A persistent simulation clock: hourly turns for politicians and corporations, frequent election and bill processing

Political dilemmas that force real responses under pressure

Prediction play on FollyMarket

Daily lottery and casual table games for downtime between campaigns

Steam and Discord account linking for progress and community access

An in-game handbook and mechanics pages so new players can learn the rules of the road

🏆 Make History or Break It

Serve your constituents or serve yourself. Uphold the system or capture it. Build a party machine, a media empire, a corporate fortress, or a courtroom dynasty.

Every election settles something. Every bill changes the board. Every deal has a price.

Battle for the Hill is free to play in Early Access. Install it, take office, and find out how far you can climb.

data.short_description: Will YOU control Congress, the Supreme Court, or the Presidency? In Battle for the Hill, a real-time multiplayer political strategy game, you’ll pass laws, shape the economy, and fight for power. Build alliances, manipulate the system, or dominate the market—every decision changes history.
data.reviews:
“Battle for the hill is a great game to get immersed in, from the multi-party system to the bill creation, no matter where you are on the political spectrum you are on there is a party for you. From right wing maga loving gop to far left socialists, you pick a side and go for the throat. Each party has their own discord so you can make friends or enemies or even frenemies. The election system is nice, raising stats, entering primaries, seeing how far you can go to win an election, the outcome is always fascinating. You can run attack ads, campaign for your colleges, change your states positions if you are elected governor, they even have gerrymandering if that is your thing. If you want to experience an exciting yet sometimes frustrating political simulation game battle for the hill is one you should try out. Will you be next? This ad review is brought to you by Yuri, join the socialist today!”
Yuri Cleary

“Battle for the Hill is a video game which is everything BUT a video game. It's a crash course on the real world via the most relevant topic in our lives: Our Government. Much like our real governments, disagreement and depression are the two things that come to mind first. However BFTH manages to circumvent reality and produce a sense of community among "politicians," causing us to think critically about issues we normally would have a safe answer for. In Battle for the Hill, unlike most simulations, the reality of "consequences" heralds players to doom or success. Resource management in cash or having to actually manage a group of people...your actions can have severe repercussions on hundreds of people and they develop situations you have to respond to. In BFTH you can be a Senator, Governor, Congress person, Party political figure such as Chair, President, SCOTUS, Cabinet, and else. There's always room for opportunity and a broom for the inactive; to be replaced by you...potentially vibrant and ambitious enough to make it to the top. BFTH isn't fun because it's a video game. It's entertaining because it's a community; Since the game has negative and positive implications for your behavior, your actions, and your decisions... BFTH becomes a real simulation. There is no total failure, but no total victory either. Everything is a perspective, and if you enjoy the realism of a world which makes you contemplate and consider the consequentialism of a "world," You'll learn more about politics here than you would from an 80 year old socialist professor at Harvard.”
James Ernest
